references.text: The Lord says that anyone who kills Cain will be avenged sevenfold. Lamech expands this protection in his own boast, claiming he will be avenged seventy-seven times.
Lamech's song where he tells of having killed a man who wounded him. This is the immediate context for verse 24, where Lamech compares his own vengeance to God's protection of Cain.

Jesus says that one should forgive not seven times, but seventy-seven times. This is a deliberate contrast to Lamech's seventy-sevenfold vengeance—where Lamech demands limitless revenge, Jesus teaches limitless forgiveness.
Encourages not to repay evil with evil, but instead to bless. This stands in contrast to Lamech's demand for excessive vengeance in Gen 4:24.
